A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TabCutMix/TabCutMixPlus study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–G are readable and support comparison despite substantial layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on memorization, synthetic-data quality, augmentation sensitivity and OOD detection, including additional datasets and generative models in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional OOD baseline comparisons and memorization-threshold analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 moves feature-correlation calculation and hierarchical clustering from inside the sample-generation loop to preprocessing before that loop. This is a limited change to the reported procedure; same-class sampling, masking and correlation measures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Adult, Default, Shoppers, Magic, Cardio, Churn Modeling and Wilt on the same tabular-generation and classification coverage. Magic results move from main Table 1 to appendix Table 7 in v2. Regression and cross-domain extensions remain future work.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds Mixup and SMOTE to the OOD comparison that contained only TabCutMix and TabCutMixPlus in v1 Table 4. Comparator membership in the retained generation-quality, IJF and GAN/VAE comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds comparisons of memorization thresholds 1/3 versus 1/2 and 1/4, plus average-rank summaries for OOD evaluation. The feature-subsampling protocol using 30%, 50%, 70% and 100% of features disappears with v1 Section 3.4. Retained experiments keep their stated splits and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The analysis suite receives focused revisions: v1's feature-dimensionality ablation and Figure 4 are removed, OOD comparisons are expanded, and v2 Figure 11 adds threshold-sensitivity checks. Dataset-size sensitivity, augmentation-ratio sensitivity, visualizations and case studies remain; the new augmentation table summarizes an existing study.

E5.justification: Both versions state five independent experimental runs, retain the fixed split-seed statement and use the same mean-plus/minus reporting practice. Added OOD rows follow that practice; changed correlation coefficients and average rankings do not introduce uncertainty estimation or significance testing.

E6.justification: v2 adds OOD baseline scores/ranks and cross-threshold correlations, and removes feature-dimensionality results. Shoppers TabDDPM+SMOTE Mem-AUC changes from 27.77 to 37.77 (v1 Table 9; v2 Table 10), while the plotted SMOTE correlation changes from 0.984 to 0.9975. Section 5.5 revises augmentation summaries, including approximately 18% to 22.06% for Shoppers at 100% augmentation. Matched benchmark-table scores otherwise remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 Proposition 3.1 moves to Appendix A as Proposition A.1, and Proposition 3.2 becomes Proposition 3.1. The optimal-score formula, assumptions, proofs and memorization-metric definitions are retained without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal claims about investigating tabular memorization, explaining it theoretically and mitigating it with TabCutMix/TabCutMixPlus. Claims to investigate feature dimensionality also remain despite removal of that experiment.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly states that the methods are designed for classification and cannot directly handle continuous regression targets. v2 also adds an interpretation of stability across memorization thresholds and discusses cross-domain transfer and real-versus-augmented indicators as future directions.

D1.justification: Appendix C explicitly places correlation calculation and clustering before sample generation, refining implementation guidance. New acknowledgements identify the computing facility used. The PyTorch/Adam setup, dataset links, XGBoost search grid and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 more explicitly presents the theoretical analysis as an application of Gu et al. (2023), including attribution in Proposition 3.1; v1 acknowledged the relationship in a footnote. The bibliography adds Langley's 'Crafting papers on machine learning.' The related-work discussion otherwise remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. v2 relocates the optimal-score proposition, removes the feature-dimensionality subsection, expands metric explanations and limitations, and adds impact and acknowledgement sections. These are localized structural and editorial revisions.

P2.justification: v2 converts the main text to two columns and extensively resizes and relocates displays. It moves Magic benchmark rows into an appendix table, adds an augmentation-ratio table, expands the OOD table and changes the four-panel correlation figure into twelve panels. Table 2's caption newly mentions TabCutMixPlus although its displayed rows remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Added threshold checks, OOD baseline comparisons and an explicit classification limitation improve validation and transparency. However, v2 removes the feature-dimensionality study while retaining claims to have investigated that factor, weakening supporting evidence. It also introduces a Table 2 caption that mentions an absent comparator. These benefits and losses leave the net overall quality change uncertain.
